title: Measles Outbreak Leads to First Child Death in Wisconsin in Decades
subtitle: Health officials warn that falling vaccination rates are making a preventable disease dangerous again.

summary.en: A young child in Wisconsin has died from measles, marking the state's first such death in 36 years. This tragic news comes as the United States experiences a nationwide rise in measles cases. Health experts note that vaccination rates have dropped below the levels needed to keep communities safe. Officials in other states, including Pennsylvania, are also dealing with serious outbreaks. Public health leaders are now urging families to ensure their children receive the necessary vaccines.
summary.zh: 威斯康辛州一名幼童因感染麻疹死亡，這是該州三十六年來首見。這起悲劇發生之際，美國全國正經歷麻疹病例激增。衛生專家指出，疫苗接種率已降至維持社區安全所需的標準以下。包括賓夕法尼亞州在內的其他州也正處理嚴重的疫情。公共衛生領袖現正呼籲家庭確保孩童接種必要的疫苗。

paragraphs.en: Health officials in Wisconsin announced a tragic development this Thursday: an infant has died after catching measles. This is the first time in 36 years that the state has recorded a death from this disease. The Wisconsin Department of Health Services did not share the exact location or other personal details, choosing to protect the privacy of the family during this difficult time. However, the coroner confirmed that measles was the cause of death.
paragraphs.zh: 威斯康辛州的衛生官員於本週四宣布了一項悲劇性的消息：一名嬰兒因感染麻疹而不幸過世。這是該州三十六年來首次記錄到死於此疾病的案例。威斯康辛州衛生服務部並未透露確切地點或其他個人細節，以保護家屬在艱難時刻的隱私。不過，驗屍官已證實死因為麻疹。

paragraphs.en: Kirsten Johnson, the secretary of the state health department, expressed deep sadness over the news. According to MedPage Today, she stated that the death of any child is a tragedy, and it is even more painful when the cause is a disease that can be prevented by a vaccine — a medical treatment that helps the body fight off specific illnesses. This event is part of a larger, worrying trend across the United States, where measles cases have been rising sharply.
paragraphs.zh: 州衛生部門秘書長強森（Kirsten Johnson）對此消息深感悲痛。根據醫學新聞網站 MedPage Today 的報導，她表示任何孩童的離世都是一場悲劇，而若死因是本可透過疫苗（一種協助人體對抗特定疾病的醫療處置）預防的疾病，則更令人心碎。此事件是美國各地麻疹病例急劇上升這一令人擔憂的趨勢之一。

paragraphs.en: For many years, the United States had successfully stopped the spread of measles. This was achieved by keeping vaccination rates high. However, recent data shows that these rates have fallen. To prevent outbreaks of this viral disease, health experts say that at least 95 percent of the population must be vaccinated. Currently, many areas have fallen below this important target. As of Thursday, Wisconsin reported 431 cases of measles. MedPage Today noted that almost all of these cases involved people who had not been vaccinated, and nine of those individuals were sick enough to require hospital care.
paragraphs.zh: 多年來，美國已成功遏止麻疹的傳播，這歸功於維持高疫苗接種率。然而，最新數據顯示接種率已下滑。衛生專家指出，為預防這種病毒性疾病爆發，至少需要百分之九十五的人口接種疫苗。目前，許多地區已低於此重要目標。截至週四，威斯康辛州通報了四百三十一例麻疹病例。MedPage Today 指出，這些病例幾乎全數未接種疫苗，其中九人病情嚴重，需要住院治療。

paragraphs.en: This situation in Wisconsin is not an isolated event. The entire country is facing a significant increase in infections. While the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has confirmed four deaths linked to measles across the nation this year, state-level reports suggest the actual numbers might be higher. For example, Pennsylvania health officials have reported five deaths this year and are currently investigating a possible sixth case. These numbers highlight the growing challenge that public health departments are facing as they try to control the spread of the virus.
paragraphs.zh: 威斯康辛州的狀況並非單一事件。全美正面臨感染人數顯著增加的挑戰。雖然美國疾病管制暨預防中心（CDC）已證實今年全國有四起與麻疹相關的死亡案例，但州級報告顯示實際數字可能更高。例如，賓夕法尼亞州的衛生官員今年已通報五起死亡案例，目前正調查第六起疑似案例。這些數字凸顯了公共衛生部門在試圖控制病毒傳播時，正面臨日益嚴峻的挑戰。

paragraphs.en: Earlier this year, other states also reported similar tragedies. In early November, New York recorded its first measles death in three decades. That event took place as the country reached a total of over 4,500 infections for the year. The scale of the problem has forced some states to take urgent action. In Pennsylvania, for instance, officials have been working hard to increase protection, administering 150,000 vaccine doses since August to help stop the virus from moving through their communities.
paragraphs.zh: 今年稍早，其他州也傳出類似的悲劇。十一月初，紐約州記錄了三十年來的首起麻疹死亡案例。該事件發生時，全國年度感染總數已超過四千五百例。問題的嚴重性迫使部分州採取緊急行動。例如在賓夕法尼亞州，官員們正努力加強防護，自八月以來已施打十五萬劑疫苗，以協助阻止病毒在社區間擴散。

paragraphs.en: Public health experts explain that the return of measles is directly connected to the drop in vaccination coverage. When fewer people are vaccinated, the virus can move easily from person to person, putting those who are too young or too sick to be vaccinated at high risk. The current outbreaks serve as a serious reminder of why these medical programs are so important for community safety.
paragraphs.zh: 公共衛生專家解釋，麻疹的捲土重來與疫苗接種覆蓋率下降有直接關聯。當接種疫苗的人數減少，病毒便能輕易地在人與人之間傳播，使那些年紀太小或因健康因素無法接種疫苗的人處於高風險之中。目前的疫情爆發是一個嚴肅的提醒，說明了為何這些醫療計畫對於社區安全如此重要。

paragraphs.en: As the number of cases continues to climb, officials are focused on both treating those who are already sick and encouraging others to get their shots. The goal is to bring vaccination rates back up to the levels required to stop the virus from spreading. For now, the focus remains on supporting the families affected by these losses and working to prevent further tragedies in the coming months. Health departments across the country continue to monitor the situation closely, hoping that increased awareness and access to vaccines will help bring the current wave of infections to an end.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著病例數持續攀升，官員們正致力於治療現有病患，並鼓勵民眾接種疫苗。目標是將疫苗接種率恢復至足以阻止病毒傳播的水準。目前，重點仍放在支持受影響的家庭，並努力在未來幾個月內防止更多悲劇發生。全國各地的衛生部門持續密切監控疫情，期望透過提高大眾意識與疫苗取得管道，能協助終結這波感染潮。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To defend oneself against or successfully resist an illness or attack.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於戰鬥語境，這裡指身體對抗病毒。文中：a medical treatment that helps the body fight off specific illnesses.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Happening only once; not part of a group or a larger trend.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 單一的、孤立的（指事件非普遍現象）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 容易誤解為「被隔離的」，這裡指事件並非單一個案。文中：This situation in Wisconsin is not an isolated event.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Spreading or passing from one place or person to another.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 傳播、移動（指病毒在人群間傳染）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作形容詞（移動的），這裡作動詞用，描述病毒傳播。文中：to help stop the virus from moving through their communities.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A sudden increase or period of a particular activity or phenomenon.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 波（指某種現象的爆發潮）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（海浪），這裡比喻疫情的爆發潮。文中：hoping that increased awareness and access to vaccines will help bring the current wave of infections to an end.

quiz.question: According to the article, what specific information did the Wisconsin Department of Health Services provide regarding the infant who died?

options.A: They confirmed the exact location where the infant contracted the disease.
options.B: They confirmed that the cause of death was measles.
options.C: They identified the family to provide support during their difficult time.
options.D: They reported that the infant had received all necessary vaccinations.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第一段，衛生部門為了保護隱私，並未透露地點或個人細節，但驗屍官確認死因為麻疹。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章明確表示未透露地點；選項 C 錯誤，因為部門選擇保護家庭隱私而非公開身份；選項 D 與事實相反，文章強調這是一起可預防的悲劇，暗示該嬰兒並未接種疫苗。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between vaccination rates and community health based on the text?

options.A: Vaccination rates have no impact on the spread of measles as long as people are treated.
options.B: Only children are at risk if the vaccination rate drops below 95 percent.
options.C: A high vaccination rate acts as a protective barrier for those who cannot be vaccinated themselves.
options.D: The government is prioritizing the treatment of sick individuals over the promotion of vaccinations.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第六段，當疫苗接種率下降，病毒容易傳播，這會讓那些年紀太小或身體太虛弱而無法接種疫苗的人處於高風險中，顯示高接種率能保護弱勢群體。選項 A 錯誤，因為疫苗接種率是防禦關鍵；選項 B 錯誤，文章並未限制僅兒童受影響；選項 D 錯誤，文章指出政府同時在進行治療與推廣接種，並未將兩者對立。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the word 'administering' mean as used in the context of the Pennsylvania health officials' actions?

options.A: Managing and distributing vaccine doses to the public.
options.B: Researching new ways to create more effective vaccines.
options.C: Investigating the causes of the recent measles outbreak.
options.D: Monitoring the health status of infected patients in hospitals.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在文章脈絡中，官員為了增加防護力而「administering」疫苗劑量，意指給予或執行接種。選項 B 錯誤，文中未提到研發新疫苗；選項 C 錯誤，調查原因與發放疫苗是不同層面的工作；選項 D 錯誤，這與監控病人無關，而是預防性的接種措施。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article?

options.A: Wisconsin is the only state in the U.S. currently struggling with measles outbreaks.
options.B: The recent rise in measles deaths is caused by a failure in medical treatment technology.
options.C: Public health officials are successfully ending the measles outbreak through new, secret methods.
options.D: Declining vaccination rates have led to a dangerous resurgence of measles, necessitating urgent public health action.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。本文主旨為探討美國麻疹疫情回升的現況，強調這與疫苗接種率下降有直接關聯，並提到各州政府正採取緊急措施應對。選項 A 錯誤，文中提到多州皆有疫情；選項 B 錯誤，問題在於接種率而非醫療技術；選項 C 錯誤，文章並未提到任何「秘密方法」，且疫情尚未結束。
